recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core follow-up is needed for FHIR-38646 unless OO later reopens BodyStructure scope wording more broadly; related R6 BodyStructure issues should be reconciled under their own keys if selected.
issue_request: FHIR-38646 was a Published/Persuasive R5 OO change request asking that BodyStructure Scope and Usage clarify that, after the FHIR-33129 restructuring, the resource can represent complex or multiple body structures and locations using included and excluded elements, can carry qualifiers such as laterality and directionality, and can be recorded outside the context of another resource.
initial_application: The Jira comment cited ef5a412, but the relevant source application found in history is 16ae4fdaa9, which added the requested BodyStructure Scope and Usage paragraphs to source/bodystructure/bodystructure-introduction.xml. The current source still includes that guidance, with later editorial refinements.
additional_context: BodyStructure is active in source/fhir.ini. The current StructureDefinition has BodyStructure.includedStructure with max '*' and BodyStructure.excludedStructure with max '*' via a content reference, matching the multiple-location premise from FHIR-33129. Later FHIR-48789 wording revised the pre-coordination sentence while retaining the included/excluded structure guidance; FHIR-54844 removed a duplicate word; and FHIR-54872 changed the neighboring Boundaries and Relationships section without undermining the FHIR-38646 scope wording.
reconciliation: No source change was necessary. The current Scope and Usage says BodyStructure can represent complex body structures and/or locations using included and excluded elements, can indicate laterality and directionality when not indicated in corresponding codes, and can be tracked outside another resource, including as a Procedure or Observation target.
